Thanks for the updated MAP, Olga. A couple of things procurement wants validated before we move the SOW:

- A succinct tokens-per-dollar sanity check for our peak flows (we've estimated 1.6M user tokens/day).
- Confirmation on caching/prefetch warm-up assumptions so our initial run won't burn budget.
- Batching thresholds you recommend for sub-200ms p95 latency.

Can you and the ops/engineering leads provide a short checklist and any supporting sims? Procurement asked for a single page that they can include in the approval packet.

Appreciate it — Dana
Sr. Product Manager, NovusCare

Subject: Re: MAP draft and evaluation plan — cost checkpoints

Dana — thanks, good capture. I've attached a ONE-PAGER (MAP-unit-cost-checklist.pdf) that covers the acceptance gates we typically put in MAPs for unit economics. High level here so procurement can paste it into the SOW: 

Summary (short):
- Baseline per-token cost (hosted model variant): $0.00035 / token (inference-only, post-commit discount reflected)
- Expected avg tokens per request: 120 (95th 420) — we’ll include distribution.
- Effective tokens/$ computed as tokens per $1 = ~2,857 tokens for baseline variant.

Critical MAP checkpoints we recommend including:
1) Prefetch warm-up plan: pre-warm cache for the top 20% of templates & prefetch KV for expected session cohorts. Expect a 10–12% cost improvement after warm-up in first 48 hours.
2) Batching policy: for sub-200ms p95 keep batch windows <= 10ms for latency-sensitive routes; permit 50–100ms windows for background/async flows (saves 15–25% tokens-$).
3) KV hit-rate gating: require a measured KV hit-rate >= 65% in the pilot week; otherwise revert to conservative timeout (no prefetch) and re-evaluate.

I'll drop the sims and an ops schedule in a follow-up from Karthik and Marcus. If procurement needs numbers in CSV for their packet I can include that as well.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-unit-cost-checklist.pdf

Olga / team — adding the ops/engineering assumptions and the quick sim results we ran against NovusCare's traffic profile. Paste of the short simulation notes below for the MAP one-pager: 

--- simulation notes ---
Model variant cost: $0.00035 / token (as Olga noted)
Avg tokens per call (observed from dev dataset): 118.7 (we'll round to 120 for planning)
Distribution: 50% calls <= 80 tokens; 30% between 80–300; 20% >300.
Batching assumptions tested:
- Latency-sensitive route: batch window 5ms, mean batch size 1.8 requests -> ~3% throughput gain vs no-batch; preserves p95 < 180ms.
- Mixed route: batch window 40ms, mean batch size 6.3 -> 22% tokens/$ improvement, p95 ~320ms (acceptable for async flows).
Caching/prefetch assumptions:
- Warm-up strategy: proactive prefetch for top-100 templates and top-10 user cohorts during first 24h; simulated warm cache hit-rate increase from 18% -> 68% over 24h.
- Expected cost delta: first 24h spike +6% then normalized to -10% average after warm-up (depends on cohort churn).
Acceptance gates to include in MAP:
1) Pilot week average tokens-per-$ measurement within +/- 15% of predicted; if > +15% risk, trigger throttling & rollback plan.
2) KV cache hit-rate >= 65% by day 2 OR show mitigation plan with cost cap.
3) Observed p95 latency for live routing <= 200ms for routes flagged as latency-sensitive.

Attached: prefet ch-warmup-sims.xlsx (summary + raw sim traces). I'll tidy and add a CSV for procurement.

Karthik
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick operational plan and timeline for the MAP acceptance checks (so this can be pasted into the mutual action plan timeline):

- Day 0 (deploy pilot config): enable prefetch for top-100 templates, batch policy pinned (latency routes = 5ms window, async = 40ms).
- Day 0–2: collect traces, measure KV hit-rate and tokens-per-request. Karthik's sim suggests we should see KV hit-rate >= 60% by end of day 1; target >=65% day 2.
- Day 3: preliminary tokens/$ report (CSV attached: novuscare-procurement-costsheet.csv) for procurement packet.
- Day 7: MAP acceptance checkpoint meeting — review tokens/$, observed p95 latency, and confirm roll to broader traffic.

If any gate fails we have a fallback: revert prefetch, cut async batch window to 10ms, and apply a soft rate limit on non-critical routes while we iterate.

Dana — happy to run a 30-minute readout with procurement once you have internal sign-off.

Regards,
Marcus
Customer Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference
